title: 2 Peter Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Peter chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Peter Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Peter Chapter 3.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The commandment of us the apostles
Words spoken by the holy prophets
Scoffers walking after their own lusts
questions.correctAnswer: Words spoken by the holy prophets
questions.explanation: This is correct because the mention of the words spoken by the holy prophets appears in 2 Peter 3:2 before any other option.

questions.question: What does Peter stir up by way of remembrance?
questions.correctAnswer: Your pure minds
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in 2 Peter 3:1, where it mentions stirring up your pure minds.

questions.question: Who does Peter refer to when he mentions 'the holy prophets'?
questions.correctAnswer: The prophets
questions.explanation: This is correct because the text in 2 Peter 3:2 mentions 'the holy prophets' directly.

questions.question: What will happen in the last days according to 2 Peter 3?
questions.correctAnswer: Scoffers will come
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in 2 Peter 3:3, which notes that scoffers will come walking after their own lusts.

questions.question: What do the scoffers question in 2 Peter 3?
questions.correctAnswer: The promise of his coming
questions.explanation: This is correct because 2 Peter 3:4 explicitly states that they say, 'Where is the promise of his coming?'.

questions.question: What do the scoffers claim about the state of things since the fathers fell asleep?
options: All things continue as they were
questions.correctAnswer: All things continue as they were
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in 2 Peter 3:4 which mentions that all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation.

questions.question: What are the scoffers willingly ignorant of?
questions.correctAnswer: The word of God
questions.explanation: This is correct according to 2 Peter 3:5, which states they are willingly ignorant of the word of God.

questions.question: By what means were the heavens and earth created according to 2 Peter 3?
options: By the hands of the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: By the word of God
questions.explanation: This is correct as 2 Peter 3:5 mentions that by the word of God, the heavens were of old.

questions.question: How did the world that then was perish?
questions.correctAnswer: By flood
questions.explanation: This is correct because 2 Peter 3:6 states that the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished.

questions.question: What does Peter say he is writing in this second epistle?
options: To warn about the end times
questions.correctAnswer: To stir up remembrance
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in 2 Peter 3:1 where he mentions stirring up your pure minds by way of remembrance.

questions.question: What does Peter refer to in the first verse of 2 Peter 3?
questions.correctAnswer: His first letter
questions.explanation: This is correct as the first verse refers to this being the second epistle written to stir up remembrance.

questions.question: True or False: Peter is writing this letter to stir up the minds of the beloved.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in 2 Peter 3:1 where Peter writes to stir up your pure minds.

questions.question: True or False: The scoffers are described as walking after their own desires.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is true according to 2 Peter 3:3 which says that scoffers will walk after their own lusts.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that the heavens were created by the hands of men.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This is false because 2 Peter 3:5 clearly states that the heavens were created by the word of God, not by men.

questions.question: True or False: The earth was destroyed by fire according to 2 Peter 3.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This is false because 2 Peter 3:6 states that the world perished by being overflowed with water, not by fire.

medium.title: 2 Peter Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Peter Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What are the heavens and the earth reserved for according to 2 Peter 3:7?
options: Judgment and perdition of ungodly men
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment and perdition of ungodly men
questions.explanation: The heavens and the earth are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men (2 Peter 3:7).

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 3:9 imply will happen if one repents?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be saved
questions.explanation: The Lord is not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance (2 Peter 3:9).

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 3:10 describe about the day of the Lord?
options: It will come suddenly and unexpectedly
It will be a day of peace
It will last for a thousand years
It will be a day of celebration
questions.correctAnswer: It will come suddenly and unexpectedly
questions.explanation: The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, indicating its sudden and unexpected arrival (2 Peter 3:10).

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 3:11, what should believers consider about their conduct?
options: They should be indifferent to the coming judgment
They should be holy and godly
They should live for worldly pleasures
They should ignore the teachings of the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: They should be holy and godly
questions.explanation: Seeing that all these things shall be dissolved, believers ought to be in all holy conversation and godliness (2 Peter 3:11).

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 3:12 encourage believers to do regarding the day of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Hasten unto it
questions.explanation: Believers are encouraged to look for and hasten unto the coming of the day of God (2 Peter 3:12).

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 3:8 convey about the perception of time for the Lord?
options: One day is like a thousand years to the Lord
God measures time differently than humans
God has no concept of time
questions.correctAnswer: One day is like a thousand years to the Lord
questions.explanation: Believers are reminded that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day (2 Peter 3:8).

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 3:3 describe the attitude of scoffers in the last days?
options: They will walk after their own lusts
questions.correctAnswer: They will walk after their own lusts
questions.explanation: Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts (2 Peter 3:3).

questions.question: What is the common misconception addressed in 2 Peter 3:4?
options: God does not care about the world
Everything continues as it always has
Believers are wrong to hope for God's promise
questions.correctAnswer: Everything continues as it always has
questions.explanation: The scoffers are saying, 'Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were' (2 Peter 3:4).

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 3:6 remind us about the world that existed before the flood?
options: It was a world of peace
It perished by being overflowed with water
It was untouched by God's judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It perished by being overflowed with water
questions.explanation: The world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished (2 Peter 3:6).

questions.question: 2 Peter 3:5 states that scoffers are willingly ignorant of what?
questions.correctAnswer: The creation of the world
questions.explanation: They are willingly ignorant of the fact that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth was created (2 Peter 3:5).

questions.question: The promise of God's coming is linked to what attribute of God in 2 Peter 3:9?
questions.correctAnswer: His mercy
questions.explanation: The Lord is longsuffering, not willing that any should perish, indicating His mercy (2 Peter 3:9).

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 3:10, what will happen to the elements on the day of the Lord?
options: They will melt with fervent heat
questions.correctAnswer: They will melt with fervent heat
questions.explanation: The elements shall melt with fervent heat, indicating a complete transformation (2 Peter 3:10).

questions.question: Is it true that the day of the Lord will come unexpectedly?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, which suggests it will be unexpected (2 Peter 3:10).

questions.question: Is it false that God is slack concerning His promises?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, meaning He is faithful and true to His word (2 Peter 3:9).

questions.question: Is it false that believers should live in godliness and holiness?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Believers ought to be in all holy conversation and godliness, as stated in 2 Peter 3:11.

hard.title: 2 Peter Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Peter Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 3:13, what do we look for according to God's promise?
options: new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness
the coming of Elijah before the day of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:13 states explicitly that according to His promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells.

questions.question: In 2 Peter 3:14, what qualities are believers urged to maintain to be found of Him in peace?
questions.correctAnswer: without spot, and blameless
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:14 exhorts believers to be diligent to be found in peace, without spot, and blameless, highlighting moral purity.

questions.question: What does 2 Peter 3:15 say about the Lord's longsuffering?
options: It is a sign of weakness
It is a time of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It is salvation
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:15 teaches that the longsuffering of the Lord is salvation, emphasizing His patience to allow repentance.

questions.question: According to 2 Peter 3:16, why do some wrest the scriptures?
options: Because they are unlearned and unstable
Because they are deceived by false prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are unlearned and unstable
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:16 states that unlearned and unstable people wrest the scriptures to their own destruction.

questions.question: What warning is given to believers in 2 Peter 3:17?
options: Beware lest you be led away with the error of the wicked and fall from your own steadfastness
Do not question the teachings of the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Beware lest you be led away with the error of the wicked and fall from your own steadfastness
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:17 warns believers to be cautious not to be led away by wicked error and lose their steadfastness.

questions.question: What are believers urged to grow in according to 2 Peter 3:18?
options: Grace and the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Grace and the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:18 commands believers to grow in grace and in the knowledge of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'makrothumia' (μακροθυμία) in 2 Peter 3:15 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering or patience
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'makrothumia' in 2 Peter 3:15 means longsuffering or patience, highlighting God's enduring patience with sinners.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Peter 3:10 describing the day of the Lord?
options: Simile, comparing the day of the Lord to a thief in the night
Allegory, representing time as a river
Paradox, stating the day is both near and far
questions.correctAnswer: Simile, comparing the day of the Lord to a thief in the night
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:10 uses a simile comparing the day of the Lord to a thief in the night, emphasizing suddenness and unexpectedness.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of new heavens and a new earth as seen in 2 Peter 3:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 65:17
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:17 prophesies new heavens and a new earth, which parallels the promise in 2 Peter 3:13.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse connects to the warning about scoffers in the last days found in 2 Peter 3:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Jude 1:18
questions.explanation: Jude 1:18 also warns of scoffers in the last time, connecting closely with 2 Peter 3:3's theme.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the promise of new heavens and a new earth in 2 Peter 3:13?
options: The heavens and earth being dissolved by fire
The preaching of the gospel to all nations
questions.correctAnswer: The heavens and earth being dissolved by fire
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:12 immediately precedes 3:13, describing the heavens and earth being dissolved by fire.

questions.question: What is the typological significance of the flood in 2 Peter 3:6 in relation to the day of judgment?
options: The flood typifies the final judgment by fire
The flood represents the baptism of believers
The flood symbolizes the Exodus from Egypt
The flood prefigures the coming of the Messiah
questions.correctAnswer: The flood typifies the final judgment by fire
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:6 contrasts the flood judgment by water with the coming judgment by fire, typologically linking both as divine judgments.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 3:8 use a literary inclusio to emphasize God's perspective on time?
options: By stating 'one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day'
By repeating the phrase 'day of the Lord' at start and end
By paralleling 'heavens' and 'earth' throughout the verse
questions.correctAnswer: By stating 'one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day'
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:8 uses a chiasm (a form of inclusio) to illustrate God's transcendent view of time.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Peter 3:9, the Lord is willing that none should perish but all should come to repentance.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:9 clearly states the Lord's longsuffering is because He is not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Peter 3:16 teaches that all of Paul's writings are easy to understand and never cause confusion.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:16 says some things in Paul's epistles are hard to be understood and are misinterpreted by the unlearned and unstable.

theological.title: 2 Peter Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Peter Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 3:6 teach about God's judgment on the world?
options: God judges the world through a flood that caused the previous world to perish
God allows the world to continue without judgment until the end of time
God's judgment is limited to spiritual punishment only
God's judgment is arbitrary and unpredictable
questions.correctAnswer: God judges the world through a flood that caused the previous world to perish
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:6 states that the world that then was perished by being overflowed with water, indicating God's judgment by flood.

questions.question: What doctrine about the promise of Christ's coming is taught in 2 Peter 3:9?
options: God is longsuffering and delays judgment to allow for repentance
God's promise is delayed because He is slack or inattentive
The promise of Christ's coming is symbolic and not literal
God will bring immediate judgment without warning
questions.correctAnswer: God is longsuffering and delays judgment to allow for repentance
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:9 explains that the Lord is not slack but longsuffering, not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning new creation is presented in 2 Peter 3:13?
options: Believers look forward to a new heaven and a new earth where righteousness dwells
The current heaven and earth will continue eternally without change
New creation refers only to individual spiritual renewal, not cosmic transformation
The new heaven and earth are metaphorical and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: Believers look forward to a new heaven and a new earth where righteousness dwells
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:13 states believers look for new heavens and a new earth wherein dwelleth righteousness, indicating a future cosmic renewal.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Peter 3:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:9 highlights God's longsuffering nature, showing His patience and desire for repentance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Peter 3:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Eternity
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:8 teaches that one day with the Lord is as a thousand years and vice versa, emphasizing God's eternal nature.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 3:10 connect to Old Testament prophetic themes about the day of the Lord?
options: It echoes prophetic imagery of cosmic judgment and destruction
It denies any future judgment and focuses only on present blessings
It presents the day of the Lord as a continuous season of peace
It limits the day of the Lord to Israel's national restoration only
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes prophetic imagery of cosmic judgment and destruction
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:10 describes heavens passing away and elements melting, themes common in Old Testament prophecy about the day of the Lord.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Peter 3:15-16 relate to Pauline epistles and their theological themes?
options: It affirms Paul's teaching on the patience of God as salvation
It criticizes Paul for difficult theology
It claims Paul's writings are irrelevant to Christian doctrine
It suggests Paul's letters contradict apostolic teaching
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms Paul's teaching on the patience of God as salvation
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:15 refers to Paul’s writings about the longsuffering of the Lord as salvation, affirming their doctrinal value.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Peter 3:7 and 3:10 teach about God's final judgment?
options: God will judge the ungodly by fire, dissolving the present heavens and earth
God's judgment is limited to spiritual condemnation without physical destruction
The present heavens and earth will remain unchanged after judgment
Final judgment is symbolic and not a literal fire
questions.correctAnswer: God will judge the ungodly by fire, dissolving the present heavens and earth
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:7 and 3:10 describe the present heavens and earth being reserved for fire and being dissolved by fervent heat at judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Peter 3:11 and 3:14 teach about Christian sanctification?
options: Believers should live holy and blameless lives in light of future judgment
Sanctification is optional because judgment is uncertain
Christians are justified but not called to live godly lives
Sanctification is unnecessary because salvation is by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should live holy and blameless lives in light of future judgment
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:11 calls for holy living because of dissolution of the world, and 3:14 urges diligence to be found without spot and blameless.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Peter 3:3 and 3:17 teach about false teaching and perseverance in faith?
options: Scoffers following lusts can lead believers away from steadfastness, so vigilance is necessary
False teachers are harmless and do not affect believers’ faith
Perseverance in faith is guaranteed without effort
Scoffers are a minor concern and do not affect the church
questions.correctAnswer: Scoffers following lusts can lead believers away from steadfastness, so vigilance is necessary
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:3 warns of scoffers, and 3:17 urges believers to beware lest they fall from their steadfastness through wicked error.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Peter 3:4-7 shows God is inactive because creation remains unchanged. What does 2 Peter 3:4-7 actually teach?
options: God actively sustains and will judge creation, despite appearances of continuity
God is indifferent to creation and allows it to persist without purpose
Creation is eternal and unchanging apart from God
God's judgment is already completed and no future judgment will occur
questions.correctAnswer: God actively sustains and will judge creation, despite appearances of continuity
questions.explanation: Verses 4-7 teach that scoffers ignore God's sustaining word and the reserved judgment by fire that will dissolve the current heavens and earth.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Peter 3:1 teach about the purpose of apostolic writing?
options: To stir up pure minds by remembrance of prophetic and apostolic teaching
To introduce new doctrines conflicting with previous revelation
To primarily entertain rather than instruct believers
To prove that previous prophecy was incorrect
questions.correctAnswer: To stir up pure minds by remembrance of prophetic and apostolic teaching
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:1 states the epistle is written to stir up pure minds by way of remembrance of previous teaching.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Peter 3:16 regarding Scripture and its interpretation?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:16 notes that Paul wrote according to the wisdom given to him, highlighting divine wisdom in Scripture.

questions.question: How does 2 Peter 3:18 advance the theme of sanctification in relation to knowledge of Christ?
options: Growth in grace and knowledge of Christ is essential for godly living
Knowledge of Christ is irrelevant to spiritual growth
Grace alone without knowledge suffices for sanctification
Sanctification is unrelated to Christ’s glory
questions.correctAnswer: Growth in grace and knowledge of Christ is essential for godly living
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:18 exhorts believers to grow in grace and knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, linking sanctification with increasing understanding.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin and error is taught in 2 Peter 3:16-17?
options: Unlearned and unstable wrest scripture leading to destruction, so believers must beware
Scriptural error is harmless and of no consequence
All interpretations of scripture are equally valid
Human error is insignificant in the face of divine truth
questions.correctAnswer: Unlearned and unstable wrest scripture leading to destruction, so believers must beware
questions.explanation: 2 Peter 3:16-17 warns that some wrest scriptures to their destruction and urges believers to beware lest they be led away with error.
